sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:142077
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 26185 of 2023

Applicant :- Kishundhari
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ram Pravesh Yadav,Sadrul Islam Jafri,Sr. Advocate
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Aditya Kumar Rai,Anjali Jaiswal,Shailendra Kumar Rai

Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri N.I.Jafri, learned Senior Advocate, assisted by Sri Ram Pravesh Yadav, learned counsel
for the applicant, Sri Shailendra Kumar Rai and Sri Aditya Kumar Rai, learned counsels for the
informant and Sri Kumwar Tejendra Bahadur, learned Aga, for the State
2.

The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No.110 of 2023, under Sections 498A and 304B IPC and Section 3/4Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Muhammadabad, District Mau during pendency of the trial.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and his family members and according to the FIR, marriage of the son of applicant was performed with the sister of the informant on 23.2.2023 and since marriage applicant and his family members started making demand of dowry and tortured her for additional demand of dowry and due to harassment made by them on 27.3.2023 she committed suicide.
It is further mentioned in FIR that applicant informed the informant about this incident on 27.3.2023 at about 17 hours.

Kishundhari vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/1579915/
1

5. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is the father-in-law of deceased and on the basis of false allegation of demand of dowry and torture, he has been made accused in the present matter.
6.

He further submits that actually deceased died within a month from her marriage, therefore, it is highly improbable that within a month of her marriage she will be tortured for demand of dowry and due to that she committed suicide.

7. He further submits that actually deceased was not happy with her marriage with the son of applicant as she was having some affair with some other boy and, therefore, only due to this reason within one month of her marriage she committed suicide.

8. He further submits that actually deceased in the afternoon of 27.3.2023 went in her room and thereafter when she could not come from her room for a considerable period of time then when applicant and his family members made enquiry then found that she hanged herself.

9. He further submits that about this incident informant was immediately informed by applicant himself and this fact has itself admitted by the informant in the FIR and after about 10.30 PM applicant informed the Police and on the information given by applicant, Police arrived and inquest report was prepared.
10. He further submits that at the time of inquest applicant was also present and after inquest, FIR of the instant case was lodged.
11. He further submits that applicant is not having any previous criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 29.3.2023, i.e., for the last about more than three months.

12. He further submits that as per the opinion of Autopsy Surgeon, deceased died due to hanging but her hyoid bone was found fractured however, after considering this fact Autopsy Surgeon opined that she died due to hanging, therefore, prima facie at this stage it appears that deceased committed suicide.
13.

Per contra learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that deceased died within one month of her marriage in her matrimonial home under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry,
therefore, applicant being father-in-law cannot be escaped from his liability.

14. Learned counsel for the informant further pointed out that even as per applicant, deceased died in the afternoon of about 3.00 PM but he informed the Police at about 22.30 hours and this fact shows the conduct of applicant.

He further submits that although Doctor, who conducted the post mortem, opined that deceased died due to hanging but her hyoid bone was found fractured,
therefore, homicidal death cannot be ruled out at this stage.

He next submits that since marriage there was demand of dowry and immediately after marriage applicant and his family members started harassing the deceased for demand of dowry and after her death they started making the Kishundhari vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/1579915/
2 allegation of bad character of the deceased therefore, considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case, applicant, who is although father-in-law of deceased, should not be released on bail.
15.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

16. From the record it reflects that applicant is the father-in-law of deceased and his daughter-in-law died within one month from the date of her marriage in her matrimonial home and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but admittedly applicant himself informed about the alleged suicide committed by deceased to the informant and he also informed the Police and on his information Panchayatnama was conducted.

17. Although, from the Panchayatnama it appears that applicant informed the Police after about more than seven hours from the time of knowledge of alleged commission of suicide committed by his daughter-in-law but in the meantime, at about 5.00 PM he had already informed the informant.

18. Further, although hyoid bone of the deceased was found fractured at the time of autopsy but according to the Autopsy Surgeon, she died due to hanging and at this stage opinion of autopsy surgeon cannot be doubted.
19. Admittedly, applicant is the father-in-law of deceased and there is no specific allegation against him and as deceased died within one month of her marriage, therefore, arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant cannot be completely brushed aside at this stage.

20. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
21. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

22. Let the applicant-Kishundhari be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
23. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

Kishundhari vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/1579915/
3 24.

It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 18.7.2023 SKM  Kishundhari vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/1579915/
